To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we present a new estimator for the probability of truthful response, (b) we present a technique to make pairwise comparisons between sensitive questions, (c) we present an estimator of Pearson’s correlation coefficient, and (d) we present an asymptotically unbiased estimator of the variance of the estimator of Pearson’s coefficient.

the Hopkins randomization device can be used to derive unbiased estimators of the proportions of respondents who answer truthfully and untruthfully, and a correlation estimator for the Pearson product moment correlation coefficient, when the randomization response technique is employed in situations where the responses to the questions of interest follow a multinomial probability model.

the Pearson correlation estimator is a useful technique for measuring the strength of the linear relationship between variables when multinomial data are observed according the randomization response protocol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of estimators for a variety of situations involving the use of randomized-response techniques in the presence of multinomial data.
the estimation of means, proportions, and correlation coefficients in the context of randomized response data.
the development of statistical methods for the analysis of randomized-response data when the response variable is multinomially distributed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multinomial model is a viable alternative to the traditional binomial model for the analysis of randomized response data, especially when there are two or more sensitive questions of interest.
the multinomial randomized response model is a useful technique for analyzing sensitive data.
the multinomial model is a useful tool for analyzing randomized-response data, especially when the sensitive information being elicited is categorical.

the multinomial randomized response model provides a very effective tool in the analysis of sensitive survey data.
